value: A `/restart` skill CC fires on itself: it measures what is behind this session, closes the boundary the way a boundary is closed (a slate through the saveslate door), and then hands off -- either by asking the inner loop to bring this session back, or by standing a new instance up beside it. One word, and the session is on the new build with its continuity written down.

value.what: cairn restart cycles the SYSTEM -- the sibling name. Akien ruled the boundary on 2026-09-22: that one does NOT restart the running cc instance(s); this one is the only thing that touches a CC session.

the dispatcher resolves an instance address -- `cairn cc.1 restart`. The third name. /restart fires `cairn cc restart` on instance 0, so it does not wait on that ticket, but the spawn branch's report reads better once `cairn cc.1 restart` resolves.
the verb this skill composes -- status|now|fresh|onexit|spawn|standdown|clear, landed 2026-09-22 in commits da6f8b01 and 6261e14d.
the door the boundary is closed through -- step 2, and the abort condition.

value.text: So next we build that out. cairn restart and cairn cc.x restart and slash restart. We only need to have you around to supervise the process the first time. Once we know it works we don't have to do any of that. ... No, cairn restart does not restart the running cc instance(s). Otherwise yes, approved all the way to proved.

MEASURED, and it decides which branch gets exercised first: every session alive today was launched by a superclaude that still exec'd claude (the loop landed in da6f8b01, after they started), so `cairn cc restart status` reports NONE for all of them and the FIRST firing of /restart takes the spawn branch. The loop branch stays unmeasured until a session launched after that commit fires it -- which is exactly the supervised first run Akien described.
